claims.claim: (a) The spec claims the home page discloses the every-visit ping.
claims.evidence: Spec 280-281: "That is why the home page names it." Spec 382 (Known limits): "**Release Health pings on every visit**, not only on a crash. The home-page copy says so." But the copy it points to (265-267) says "The player sends anonymous crash statistics" - no word about visits, and it names "The player" as the sender. So the claim is made, and the copy's words do not carry it.

claims.claim: (b) web/instrumentation-client.ts runs on every route, including `/`, so the ping is sent from the home page before anyone opens the player.
claims.evidence: Bundled docs (next 16.3.6): web/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/instrumentation-client.md:6 "...other side-effects that run before your application becomes interactive."; :8 "place the file in the **root** of your application"; 01-app/02-guides/analytics.md:13 "...runs before your application's frontend code starts executing. This is ideal for setting up global analytics, error tracking, or performance monitoring tools." The docs never say "every route" in those words; the source settles it: web/node_modules/next/dist/client/app-next-turbopack.js:11 "const instrumentationModules = require('../lib/require-instrumentation-client');" and :15 "hydrate(instrumentationModules, assetPrefix);" - the one App Router client entry, so it runs on `/` and `/play` alike (app-next.js:9-10 does the same for webpack). Sentry side (docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/configuration/releases/, via WebFetch): "JavaScript Browser SDKs track sessions by default." / "A session starts on page load and continues across client-side navigations. A hard reload or navigation starts a new session." / "Before SDK version 11, the SDK started a new session on each client-side navigation by default." getsentry/sentry-javascript develop, packages/browser/src/integrations/browsersession.ts: setup calls startSession({ ignoreDuration: true }) and sends it with captureSession() inside whenIdleOrHidden(...) - from whichever page loaded first, `/` included. This also answers the spec's own plan-time item "That the browser SDK sends Release Health sessions by default" (line 392): yes, per the docs.

claims.evidence: The sentence spans lines 9-10, not 9 alone: web/app/page.tsx:9 "        Open a score from your own computer, read it as standard notation, and play along. claims.claim: (a) Sentry's project-creation flow offers an alert option such as "Alert me on high priority issues" by default.
claims.evidence: getsentry/sentry master, static/app/views/projectInstall/issueAlertOptions.tsx (via WebFetch): "[RuleAction.DEFAULT_ALERT, t('Alert me on high priority issues')]", "tct('When there are more than [threshold][metric] a unique error [interval]', ...)", "[RuleAction.CREATE_ALERT_LATER, t(\"I'll create my own alerts later\")]", and the default "DEFAULT_ISSUE_ALERT_OPTIONS_VALUES = { alertSetting: RuleAction.DEFAULT_ALERT, ... }". Sentry changelog 2024-09-16 (sentry.io/changelog/issue-alerts-now-have-priority-conditions): "Default alerts in Sentry have been updated to use our new high priority conditions."

claims.claim: (b) Warning-level issues get medium priority by default, so a high-priority-only alert skips them.
claims.evidence: docs.sentry.io/product/issues/issue-priority/ (via WebFetch): "**High**: Issues that are likely to be actionable and require immediate attention, such as `ERROR` and `FATAL` events." / "**Medium**: Issues that are likely to be actionable and require attention in the near future, including `WARNING` events." Consequence (reasoned): every warning in the spec - E103 (line 158), E101/E102 (159), E602 (157), E601/E603 (171) - opens as a medium issue and never fires the default rule; that includes the E103 warning setup step 5 waits for. The same page adds that for "Python or JavaScript projects" the enhanced priority considers "whether or not the error is handled", so even handled error-level reports (every reportError call) may rate below high - the direction is not documented (unverified).

claims.claim: (c) The free Developer plan includes issue alerts by email.
claims.evidence: sentry.io/pricing (via WebFetch): the Developer plan's feature bullets include "Alerts and notifications via email" (present on all four plans); "Alerts and notifications via integrated tools" starts at Team.

claims.claim: (d) The exact trigger name "A new issue is created".
claims.evidence: docs.sentry.io/product/monitors-and-alerts/alerts/create-alerts/ and /product/alerts/create-alerts/issue-alert-config/ (via WebFetch) list the triggers "A new issue is created", "An issue escalates", "A resolved issue regresses", "An issue is resolved", "An event or issue activity is captured", "Seer runs on an issue and reaches the stage...". The action is "Notify on preferred channel" to "Suggested Assignees", a "Team", or a "Member", delivered "via each recipient's notification settings"; no action is named "email".

spike.what: Public docs and Sentry source only.

fix_conflicts_with_other_sections: None. Keep the new instruction inside or after step 1, so line 302 ("filled in from section 5, step 1") still points at the slugs step.
fix_correction: Two wording corrections. (1) The project-creation form cannot create this rule: its only choices are "Alert me on high priority issues" (default), "When there are more than [threshold][metric] a unique error [interval]" and "I'll create my own alerts later". So the step should read: when creating the project, choose "I'll create my own alerts later"; then create one alert with the trigger "A new issue is created", no level filter, and the action "Notify on preferred channel" -> Member: leocaseiro (on the Developer plan it arrives by email). (2) Say "Notify on preferred channel -> Member", not "email leocaseiro" - the alert form has no action named email.
notes: Trade-off for the person, not a correction: the default rule also fires when an EXISTING issue becomes high priority (escalation). A new-issue-only rule drops that; the same rule can also take "An issue escalates" and "A resolved issue regresses" if wanted. Alerts use no event quota.

claims.claim: An E103 event arrives whether or not source maps resolve (reasoned).
claims.evidence: Reasoned: ingestion does not depend on source maps; they only change how the stack is shown. Sentry's troubleshooting page (docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/sourcemaps/troubleshooting_js/, via WebFetch) implies it: it describes a "Sentry not part of build pipeline" error shown when deployed code lacks Debug IDs, and says to "Verify your artifacts are being uploaded to Sentry. You can find them at [Settings] > Projects > Select your project > [Source Maps]." Nuance: a HARD upload failure stops the build by default in Sentry's bundler plugins (@sentry/esbuild-plugin 5.4.0 README: "By default, the plugin will simply throw an error, thereby stopping the bundling process."); whether the Next.js Turbopack post-build upload does the same is unverified. A SOFT failure (maps uploaded but not matched to the code) passes step 5 unseen. And since preview, CI and local builds skip the upload (line 295), the first production deploy is the first time the upload runs at all.

fix_conflicts_with_other_sections: n/a (FYI). An implied fix would add to step 5: the E103 event's stack shows our source file names (for example PlayerShell.tsx) with the code around the line, and the project's Source Maps settings page lists the release - no conflict with section 4.

claims.evidence: The project ships on Vercel Hobby (docs/decisions/2026-07-08-fe-nextjs-vercel-aws-bff-adr.md:33 "Ship on Vercel Hobby ($0, best DX)"). Without Web Analytics, only Observability remains: vercel.com/docs/observability/observability-plus Limitations table, "Data Retention | Hobby: 12 hours" and "CDN Requests | No breakdown by path"; vercel.com/docs/observability counts requests, not visits ("1 CDN request event if it's a static asset."). So no month-long visit count exists. Web Analytics would give one, but needs enabling in the dashboard plus @vercel/analytics plus <Analytics /> in the root layout (vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart: "Once your app is deployed, it will start tracking visitors and page views."); free on Hobby with "50,000 events / month included" and "Reporting Window | 1 Month" (vercel.com/docs/analytics/limits-and-pricing).
